recs.subject: act
errors: Version 2: 'The bracket opens toward the numbers that count' is a misleading rule — parentheses also open toward the interval, so opening direction does not distinguish included from excluded endpoints.

Version 2 (wording risk, not a hard falsehood): distractor feedback 'This flips both ends. 2 is out and 7 are in.' (Block 5) and 'This flips both ends: 2 is in and 7 is out.' (Block 8) can be misread as describing the flipped distractor, which would be false; they only work as restatements of the correct endpoints, and the phrasing is confusing for a low-flexibility reader.
recs.objective_note: Both versions teach the same objective: writing inequalities like 2 < x ≤ 7 as (2, 7] with correct brackets, infinity always taking a parenthesis, and matching notation to number-line graphs. Version 1 extends to solving a compound inequality to produce a solution set — an extension of the same objective, not a drift; Version 2 stays on notation/graph matching.
